1  ORDER

This Criminal Revision Petition has been filed to set aside the order passed in Crl.M.P.No.1797 of 2017 in C.C.No.146 of 2002 on the file of the learned Judicial Magistrate, Karaikudi dated 12.01.2018 and thereby dismissed the petition seeking for further investigation for the offence under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C.
2.The petitioner is the de-facto complainant.

She lodged a complaint as against her husband and in-laws and the same was registered in Crime No.6 of 2001 on the file of the respondent police for the offence under Section 498A, 494 and 406 IPC and Section 4 of Dowry Prohibition Act.
3.The respondent police after completion of investigation, filed final report and the same has been taken cognizance by the trial Court.

However, A1 failed to appear before the trial Court and as such,
the trial Court had split up the case and proceeded as against A2 and A3 in C.C.No.146 of 2002.
Again it was split up in C.C.No.115 of 2004 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis conducted trial.
After completion of prosecution witnesses, when the matter was posted for 313 of Cr.P.C questioning.
Again the petitioner filed a petition seeking further investigation.
However, the trial Court had dismissed the said petition.

Aggrieved by the same, the petitioner has preferred a revision before this Court in Crl.R.C(MD)No.468 of 2012 and this Court had set aside the order passed by the trial Court and directed the respondent police to entrust the further investigation with a competent superior officer and further, directed the respondent police to expedite the further investigation and filed a report.
Accordingly, the superior officer conducted further investigation in Crime No.6 of 2001 and filed a report.
4.On perusal of the said report, it revealed that already they inspected the matrimonial home and found nothing was alleged by the de-facto complainant.
At that juncture, again the petitioner filed another application seeking further investigation under Section 173(8) of Cr.P.C and the same was dismissed by the trial Court.
Therefore, this Court finds no infirmity or illegality in the order passed by the trial Court.
Hence, this Criminal Revision Petition stands dismissed.
However, the trial https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis Court is directed to complete the trial within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
